extracted.intended_audience: Stakeholders and members of the public submitting comments on DOE rulemakings (manufacturers, trade associations, NGOs, researchers, and individual commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for participating in and submitting effective public comments and oral input for Department of Energy rulemakings (especially energy efficiency and electricity-sector rules). Covers submission channels, participation opportunities, and DOE-specific evidence and analysis to include in comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments may be submitted through: Regulations.gov website, Email, Postal mail, Hand delivery/courier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists acceptable channels for filing comments; follow agency docket instructions for formatting, deadlines, and docket numbers when using any of these methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary platform — Regulations.gov docket review
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in rulemakings by viewing Federal Register notices, supporting documents, and public comments in the rulemaking docket found on Regulations.gov, a web-based repository of federal regulatory documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Regulations.gov docket to find the official notice, supporting technical documents, and existing public comments; filing via Regulations.gov places your comment in the public docket for agency consideration and public review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation options — public meetings and webinars
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE holds public meetings and webinars related to rulemakings to gather information and present analysis results, with stakeholders invited to comment on design options. Anyone can participate either in-person or via a webinar, and in-person participants are allowed to make oral presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend and present at public meetings/webinars to deliver oral comments and engage directly with DOE staff; use these venues to highlight key evidence and to comment on design alternatives presented by DOE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific statutory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: For energy efficiency standards, electricity sector, and DOE rulemakings: cite specific statutory authority (Energy Policy and Conservation Act, FERA, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground comments in the relevant enabling statutes to show how proposed approaches align with or deviate from statutory requirements and DOE's legal duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with the Technical Support Documents (TSDs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with the technical support documents (TSDs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically analyze TSD assumptions, data sources, and methodologies; point to specific TSD sections and provide corrections, alternative data, or improved methods where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address energy savings calculations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify errors or alternative assumptions in energy savings estimates, provide corrected calculations or data, and explain how changes affect the rule’s projected benefits and cost-effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide manufacturer impact data (for appliance standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide manufacturer impact data (for appliance standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit empirical cost, engineering, capacity, or production data from manufacturers to inform feasibility, industry impacts, and lead times; quantify impacts when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include life-cycle cost analyses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide or critique analyses of total cost of ownership for consumers over product lifetimes, including energy costs, maintenance, and performance impacts; explain assumptions and sensitivity to key parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address consumer impact — energy bills, performance, and choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Address consumer impact (energy bills, product performance, choice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the proposed standard would affect consumers’ energy bills, product performance, upfront costs, and available choices; include distributional impacts across consumer groups if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference DOE's National Impact Analysis (NIA) methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference DOE's NIA (National Impact Analysis) methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If critiquing or supplementing DOE’s national-level analyses, map comments to NIA inputs/assumptions and provide alternative parameter values, data, or modeling approaches consistent with NIA structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with discount rate assumptions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment on the appropriateness of discount rates used in consumer and national analyses; provide evidence for alternate rates and show effect on present-value estimates and cost-effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address technology substitution scenarios
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss likely or plausible technology substitution paths and their timing; provide data or modeling to support scenarios and explain implications for energy savings and market impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite Test Procedure data where applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite Test Procedure data where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where relevant, provide or critique test-procedure-derived performance data, explain testing limitations, and recommend measurement or test-procedure changes if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow DOE Process Rule stages when commenting (10 CFR § 430)
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE's "Process Rule" sets out the procedures for energy efficiency standard rulemaking, including: Framework documents, Preliminary analyses, NOPR, Final rule. Comments at each stage have distinct functions and influence opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor comments to the procedural stage — early-stage comments (framework/preliminary analyses) can shape design and assumptions, comments on the NOPR should address the proposed regulatory text and quantified analyses, and late-stage comments should focus on remaining errors or new information prior to final rule.
